content: Do we actually have a reason for not depending on mathlib given how well supported that ecosystem is? Every reason I can think of falls flat when I talk to Derek Dreyer or Ilya Sergey for example. We just end up not benefitting from all that math or requiring extra and error-prone configuration steps.

Yes. Aside from the fact that mathlib is not necessary*, Iris-Lean benefits from having only stable dependencies, and not clashing with mathlib versions that are out of sync (latest vs nightly, for example).

*We have copy-pasted a little mathlib code, but it's on my list of things to do to get that moved to batteries.
Uhh, you can simply track mathlib stable. It only changes once a month, which is the same frequency as lean stable toolchain changes.
What happens when I want to use Iris-Lean in a project that uses mathlib nightly
You'd have a toolchain mismatch regardless. Cache will complain that your lean toolchain doesn't match mathlib's toolchain. Iris currently tracks stable lean toolchains.
5 messages were moved here from #iris-lean > Bi-entailment and generalized rewriting by Shreyas Srinivas.

I just checked this. When I create an iris + mathlib master dependent project, lake upgrades the project's lean toolchain to 4.30.0-rc1. There are incompatibilities with iris which is still at v4.28.0. So you get an error message like below:

lakefile.toml

name = "IrisAndMathDependentProject"
version = "0.1.0"
defaultTargets = ["IrisAndMathDependentProject"]

[[lean_lib]]
name = "IrisAndMathDependentProject"

[[require]]
name = "iris"
git = "https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean.git"
rev = "master"

[[require]]
name = "mathlib"
git = "https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4.git"
rev = "master"

Iris error with mathlib stable dependent project

`/home/shreyas/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.30.0-rc1/bin/lake setup-file /home/shreyas/Projects/Lean/IrisAndMathDependentProject/IrisAndMathDependentProject/Basic.lean -` failed:

stderr:
⚠ [8272/8329] Replayed Iris.Algebra.OFE
warning: ./src//Iris/Algebra/OFE.lean:146:0: Definition `Iris.OFE.ofDiscrete` of class type must be marked with `@[reducible]` or `@[implicit_reducible]`
warning: ./src//Iris/Algebra/OFE.lean:635:0: Definition `Iris.COFE.ofDiscrete` of class type must be marked with `@[reducible]` or `@[implicit_reducible]`
warning: ./src//Iris/Algebra/OFE.lean:675:11: instance `Iris.COFE.OFunctor.cofe` must be marked with `@[reducible]` or `@[implicit_reducible]`

Even if lake doesn't throw lean toolchain mismatch errors, it will favour mathlib's toolchain and replace your current project toolchain with mathlib's. So you end up with version incompatibilities anyway

If instead iris depended on mathlib, it would have to match some mathlib toolchain to pass CI. Then when you add an iris dependency, the correpsonding mathlib dependency would be pulled in and you would have no toolchain mismatch issues.

Sure, toolchain mismatches on Iris Lean master vs mathlib master are expected as you say. But I guess you can depend on the version of mathlib for the toolchain of Iris Lean. (e.g. the v4.28.0 tag).

Shreyas Srinivas said:

Iris currently tracks stable lean toolchains.

I think it is a good point that it would be nice if Iris Lean would be faster with updating to new Lean versions (maybe even to rc versions if mathlib does that?) But I don't think there is currently the manpower for it. If people start to depend on Iris Lean and Mathlib at the same time, I imagine that there will be a stronger push to keep Iris Lean more up to date. Until then, the current way things work seems fine to me.

Michael Sammler said:

Sure, toolchain mismatches on Iris Lean master vs mathlib master are expected as you say. But I guess you can depend on the version of mathlib for the toolchain of Iris Lean. (e.g. the v4.28.0 tag).

In which case depending on mathlib would cause no issues.

Ah I also just tested it locally, and it seems like having dependencies that have different mathlib versions is not as bad as I remember.

We just end up not benefitting from all that math

In my experience the amount of mathlib we need is minimal, and that overlap is not math-specific so it should be moved to batteries anyways.
